## Definitions

- [statement] Neuromelanin-sensitive MRI is an emerging candidate biomarker, but the strong performance of a small retrospective 7T study does not establish its accuracy in premotor, equivocal or atypical cases: its authors explicitly called for studies in those populations. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-024-00631-3 · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET

## How it works

- [statement] Conventional structural MRI identifies vascular damage, masses and patterns of atrophy that can cause or help distinguish parkinsonism; ordinary anatomical sequences have limited ability to identify the dopaminergic deficit itself. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6280219/ · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] In the 2014 swallow-tail MRI study, retrospective-cohort diagnostic accuracy was 96% on diagnostic scans and fell to 91% when non-diagnostic scans were included; scan quality therefore materially affected the reported performance. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3977922/ · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] A 2024 retrospective 7T neuromelanin MRI study included 21 PD patients, 13 essential-tremor patients and 18 controls; substantia nigra pars compacta total volume distinguished PD from the pooled non-PD group with reported sensitivity 100% and specificity 96.8%. These are within-study results. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-024-00631-3 · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Presynaptic dopamine-transporter imaging supports distinguishing essential tremor from neurodegenerative parkinsonism; an abnormal DaTscan is not specific for idiopathic Parkinson’s disease and cannot reliably separate it from atypical degenerative parkinsonism. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/ · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET · also: https://www.apdaparkinson.org/article/what-is-a-datscan-and-should-i-get-one/, https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/022454s010lbl.pdf
- [statement] Conventional structural MRI generally does not confirm PD, but can identify alternative structural causes or findings suggesting atypical parkinsonism; its sensitivity for atypical syndromes is limited early in disease. (medium confidence) — https://www.apdaparkinson.org/article/what-is-a-datscan-and-should-i-get-one/ · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET · also: https://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/58/12/1888
- [statement] FDG-PET measures regional cerebral glucose metabolism and can support differentiating parkinsonian syndromes using disease-associated patterns; this is a different biological readout from presynaptic dopamine-terminal imaging. (medium confidence) — https://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/58/12/1888 · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10423182/, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6280219/, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10072-022-06166-w, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/
- [statement] The EANM/SNMMI guideline describes fluorodopa PET as a presynaptic dopaminergic assessment and notes that atypical parkinsonian syndromes usually cannot be separated from idiopathic PD with this technique; FDG-PET instead evaluates metabolic patterns. PET tracers should therefore not be treated as interchangeable tests. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/ · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET · also: https://jnm.snmjournals.org/content/58/12/1888
- [statement] PET measures depend on the tracer: fluorodopa uptake reflects tracer influx and decarboxylation in presynaptic dopamine assessment, whereas FDG-PET maps regional glucose metabolism and disease-related metabolic patterns. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/ · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6280219/
- [statement] The EANM/SNMMI guideline warns that DAT binding reaches a floor later in disease, weakening its correlation with further clinical progression; scan signal should not be treated as a universally linear progression measure. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/ · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] The DATSCAN label (revised 11/2022) states that its effectiveness as a screening or confirmatory test, and for monitoring disease progression or response to therapy, has not been established. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/022454s010lbl.pdf · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] In the DATSCAN label's two multicenter studies of 284 adult patients with suspected parkinsonian syndromes, the clinical reference category parkinsonian syndromes (PS) comprised Parkinson's disease, multiple system atrophy and progressive supranuclear palsy, and the label states that DATSCAN imaging was not designed to distinguish among these conditions. (low confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/022454s010lbl.pdf · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] NICE guideline NG71 (published 19 July 2017) recommends considering 123I‑FP‑CIT SPECT for people with tremor if essential tremor cannot be clinically differentiated from parkinsonism, and says not to use PET in the differential diagnosis of parkinsonian syndromes except in the context of clinical trials. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] NICE guideline NG71 (published 19 July 2017) says not to use structural MRI to diagnose Parkinson's disease, while structural MRI may be considered in the differential diagnosis of other parkinsonian syndromes. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] In the EANM/SNMMI guideline, early idiopathic Parkinson’s disease typically shows reduced uptake first in the posterior putamen opposite the symptomatic side, with greater putaminal than caudate involvement; this is a typical pattern rather than a disease-specific signature. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/ · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] The EANM/SNMMI guideline interprets persistent scans without dopaminergic deficit as evidence against idiopathic PD; Palermo and colleagues instead reported eight older-onset levodopa-responsive cases with initially normal scans, two later abnormal. Their cases lacked pathological confirmation, so this is an attributed limitation rather than proof that normal scans commonly miss PD. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/ · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9092727/
- [statement] A 2023 retrospective clinical series of 156 patients referred for suspected atypical parkinsonism found overall FDG-PET classification accuracy of 74%, using follow-up clinical diagnosis rather than autopsy as the reference; the reader had access to prior dopamine-transporter imaging. The authors acknowledge reference-standard bias and missing histopathological confirmation. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10423182/ · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] DaTscan uses iodine-123 ioflupane SPECT to visualize striatal dopamine transporter availability; it is an adjunct to other diagnostic evaluations rather than a standalone disease identification test. (medium confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/022454s010lbl.pdf · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/
- [statement] For dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), the DATSCAN label reports, in 55 patients clinically diagnosed with DLB or Alzheimer's disease and compared with autopsy diagnosis, sensitivity of 80% (95% CI 61% to 92%) and specificity of 92% (95% CI 74% to 99%); the label derives this evidence from the scientific literature. (low confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/022454s010lbl.pdf · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] A meta-analysis of nigrosome-1 appearance on MRI included nineteen studies with a total of 1508 participants (903 idiopathic PD patients and 605 healthy controls) and reported pooled sensitivity 0.94 (95 percent CI 0.93-0.96) and specificity 0.90 (95 percent CI 0.88-0.92) for differentiating idiopathic PD from healthy adults; the comparison was with healthy adults rather than other parkinsonian syndromes. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32668370/ · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET

## Facts and statements

- [statement] DAT-SPECT interpretation requires checking potentially interfering drugs and structural imaging: cocaine, amphetamines and methylphenidate can markedly reduce tracer binding, while anatomic lesions and atrophy can alter apparent striatal binding or shape. Medication changes require clinician-directed preparation. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/ · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] A 2014 primary MRI study showed that healthy nigrosome-1 can appear as a swallow-tail hyperintensity on high-resolution 3T susceptibility-weighted imaging, with this appearance lost in PD. The authors called for independent prospective validation. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3977922/ · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] The 2024 7T MRI authors identify small sample size, retrospective design and inclusion of established PD as limitations, and call for studies in equivocal PD and atypical parkinsonism; their reported accuracy should not be assumed to generalize to routine diagnostic populations. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-024-00631-3 · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] In the same 7T study, neuromelanin volume discriminated groups, whereas contrast ratio did not differ significantly between PD and non-PD groups; a result for one MRI metric should not be generalized to all neuromelanin measurements. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-024-00631-3 · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] In a retrospective study of eighty-three clinically confirmed degenerative parkinsonian cases, voxel-based FDG-PET maps added diagnostic accuracy and confidence, particularly for less experienced readers; expert-reader improvement was mainly supported by hypometabolism maps. (low confidence) — https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10072-022-06166-w · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] DAT-SPECT quantification requires attention to acquisition and processing: the EANM/SNMMI guideline cautions that specific binding ratios from different cameras, acquisition methods, processing and analyses are not directly interchangeable. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/ · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] The FDA prescribing information for DATSCAN (ioflupane I 123 injection), revised 11/2022, indicates it as an adjunct to other diagnostic evaluations for striatal dopamine transporter visualization using single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) brain imaging in adult patients with suspected parkinsonian syndromes or suspected dementia with Lewy bodies. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/022454s010lbl.pdf · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET

## Research summary — Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET

Imaging contributes complementary evidence rather than a single disease-specific answer. Dopamine-transporter SPECT identifies presynaptic dysfunction but does not reliably separate PD from atypical degenerative parkinsonism. Structural MRI helps assess alternative causes; nigrosome and neuromelanin MRI offer promising research measures whose diagnostic performance depends on population, acquisition and validation. FDG-PET examines cerebral metabolic patterns, whereas fluorodopa PET assesses presynaptic dopaminergic function. Small MRI case-control studies should not be equated with routine clinical accuracy. Drug interference, structural lesions, non-diagnostic scans and clinical rather than pathological reference standards constrain interpretation. Selected older-onset cases with initially normal DAT-SPECT further caution against absolute exclusion claims. The FDA label positions DaTscan as an adjunct to other diagnostic evaluations, and NICE NG71 recommends considering it when essential tremor cannot be clinically differentiated from parkinsonism.

## Source disagreement — Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET

EANM/SNMMI regards persistent SWEDD as unlikely idiopathic PD; Palermo et al. describe selected older-onset clinical cases with initially normal imaging and argue for possible false negatives, while acknowledging absent pathological confirmation. This is a difference in scope and interpretation, not an established general false-negative rate.
